newsitem.title: UK: Virgin takes stake in UK rugby league team.
newsitem.headline: Virgin takes stake in UK rugby league team.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Group said on Wednesday it had taken a 15 percent stake in rugby league club London Broncos.
"Quite a few people will be wondering why Virgin has chosen rugby league as its first foray into international sport -- as opposed to football, rugby union or even cricket," Branson said.

"The answer is simply that rugby league is one of Britain's fastest growing sports and has been underdeveloped in the south. But it is a great spectator sport and one day could become the main sport in the country," added Branson, who did not specify how much he was investing in the London club.
Rugby league has expanded from its traditional roots in northern England as the London Broncos and Paris St Germain joined a new European super league set up last year.
The new league, part of a lucrative deal with pay television operator BSkyB, also marked the switch of the sport to a summer game rather than a winter one.
There are also plans for the leading teams in Europe to play off against the top clubs in New Zealand and Australia.
The Broncos were born in 1994 when the management team of Australia's Brisbane Broncos took over London's second division Crusaders club.
The Broncos finished fourth last year in the European Super League. They will play in the coming season at the Stoop Memorial Ground in Twickenham, home to rugby union's Harlequins.
